reason: Whether the two consumption paths can ever be active simultaneously hinges on the outer `if (oldChildrenByKey ...)` condition and on what `indexChildrenByKey` includes — neither is visible in this hunk; if the guard is simply `if (oldChildrenByKey)` the `else if` becomes unreachable once the index exists and the claimed double-consumption cannot occur, while a per-child key guard would make it real (the claim also cites `shift()`, which only exists after the change).
